title: Beyond Deference: India’s Bangladesh Reckoning
author: Shanthie Mariet D’Souza
text:
Credit: ID 237095693 © OnePixelStudio | Dreamstime.com
On October 6, Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi called on Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi. It isn’t unusual for heads of Indian missions assigned to critical or sensitive bilateral stations to provide direct update or receive specific strategic directives during visits or consultations in New Delhi. Modi’s office maintains an active and hands-on approach to foreign policy implementation, making direct communication and briefings with key diplomatic personnel a standard part of administrative routine. However, Trivedi’s case and the circumstances of the meeting are rather unique. Trivedi was appointed as India’s high commissioner to Bangladesh in April 2026, a rare political appointment to a key neighboring diplomatic mission. A businessman and a politician of the ruling BJP from the eastern state of West Bengal, he has direct access to Modi and does not need to route his meetings through the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). His appointment to Dhaka in April 2026, replacing a career diplomat, came at a time when bilateral relations between India and Bangladesh had hit a rough patch. [...]
